output.name: Skerá — The Hanging Hawk
output.myth: Ennu made the hawk the winter the gulls stole three nets of Halla's cod and laughed at her. He cut it from red sailcloth and gave it a bone beak and two wings that never flapped. A hawk, Ennu said, is only a shadow with patience. He flew it over the nets, and the gulls went screaming off the cliffs. Then Tavo the Gale came to see what was up there and pulled hard at the string, and Ennu had to hold on with both hands. The hawk did not fall. It hangs at the top of the Windward Reach, wings out, because Hesk keeps the string wound and will not let the Gale have it. North of it sits Sekál, the Bone Gull, carved from a whale's jaw after the nets were mended, and it watches the hawk from above. To the west Skeru the Asking Raven asks the wind questions, and Tavo tugs the string to answer. When the nets are wet and the gulls come back, the hawk's shadow shows on the water. Ennu is still holding on, and his hands are never cold.
output.finding: Find Sekál, the Bone Gull, and look a fist and a half (about 14°) due south of it to find Skerá, the Hanging Hawk.
